question: Is the 2024 Agno River Basin conference abstract an earlier version of the 2026 fish survey, and does it support any station-specific Tarlac or Camiling River fish claim?

method.summary: Compared the APRU/UPLB 2024 conference-program abstract with the 2026 peer-reviewed article and its University of Glasgow dataset record. The comparison is bibliographic and aggregate-only; no sample-level crosswalk or new fish rows were created.
method.conferenceRecord: The official APRU-hosted SCL x ICHSPD 2024 Souvenir Program identifies the 6–8 August 2024 event and includes the abstract under the title 'Exploring Diversity: Fish Assemblages in the Agno River Basin, Philippines.' The abstract and listed authors were reviewed in the Abstracts section.
method.articleAndDatasetRecords: The 2026 paper and linked University of Glasgow dataset had already been reviewed in the ARB7 Paniqui station review and the national Agno basin review. This follow-up rechecked the article abstract, station table/methods and the current dataset landing-page metadata.
method.lineageAssessment: The matching first author, similar Agno fish-assemblage title and basin scope, overlapping author group, named Paniqui and Bocboc localities, and identical reported diversity-index range (0.29–1.62) suggest the 2024 abstract may present preliminary or related results. The abstract does not state a collection period, the author lists differ, its aggregate richness/composition differs from the final 2026 article, and no version, sample or station-matrix crosswalk was located. Relationship remains unconfirmed.
method.limitations: The conference abstract supplies pooled aggregate results, not a complete species checklist, station-by-taxon matrix, specimen identifiers or fish-specific observations at Paniqui. A place mentioned for water-quality comparison does not attach the basin-level fish totals to that locality. No Camiling River station is named.

conferenceAbstract.locator: APRU SCL x ICHSPD 2024 Souvenir Program, Abstracts section, entry beginning 'Exploring Diversity: Fish Assemblages in the Agno River Basin, Philippines'; conference cover gives 6–8 August 2024, Taguig City.
conferenceAbstract.reportedScope: Agno River Basin across Benguet, Pangasinan and Tarlac. Paniqui, Tarlac and Bocboc, San Carlos are named in a water-quality comparison; the abstract does not give fish-taxon-by-station results.
conferenceAbstract.reuse: No item-specific license or permission for the conference abstract was identified. Preserve citation and concise factual review notes only; no abstract prose or figures are reproduced.

laterArticle.locator: Tenio et al. (2026), abstract, section 2.1/Table 1 and fish-sampling sections 2.2–2.3.
laterArticle.citation: Tenio, K. F. C., et al. (2026). Diversity and distribution of freshwater fish in mineralized watersheds of the Agno River Basin, Northern Philippines. Watershed Ecology and the Environment, 8, 248–260. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wsee.2026.05.001
laterArticle.reportedScope: Eight source-named Agno Basin stations, including ARB7 Paniqui, Tarlac. The article reports fish sampling in July 2021 and January 2022; the season-to-month assignment conflicts with the repository metadata and remains unresolved.
laterArticle.reuse: Article identifies CC BY 4.0. The separate conference program's rights are not inferred from the article license.

linkedDataset.locator: University of Glasgow Enlighten Research Data, DOI 10.5525/gla.researchdata.2287; public metadata and file/license listing.
linkedDataset.finding: The dataset provides station coordinates and fish assemblage counts for the 2026 article. It is not a version or specimen crosswalk for the 2024 aggregate abstract.
linkedDataset.license: CC BY 4.0 per the dataset landing page.

evidenceForRelationship: Same lead author and substantially similar Agno basin fish-assemblage title.
Overlapping author group and shared Benguet–Pangasinan–Tarlac basin scope.
Both records mention Paniqui and the same 0.29–1.62 diversity-index range.
evidenceAgainstTreatingAsResolved: The conference abstract reports 19 species/12 families; the 2026 article reports 23/13.
The conference abstract says cichlids and cyprinids dominate; the later paper reports Gobiidae at 84% and Cichlidae at 11%.
The author lists differ, and the conference abstract provides no study dates, methods detailed enough to crosswalk, supplement, station matrix or sample identifiers.
No source statement confirms whether these are the same samples, an earlier analysis, or related but distinct survey data.
lineageDecision.decision: Keep both publication records distinct in the bibliography, but do not count the conference abstract as an independent survey, merge its totals with the 2026 article, or project its pooled claims to ARB7, Camiling River or another site. Seek author clarification or a primary sample-level version crosswalk.

nextActions: Add an unsent author-clarification question asking whether the 2024 conference abstract reports preliminary or different samples from the 2026 article, and how the 19/12 aggregate and family-abundance summary relate to the 23/13 final paper.
Continue Camiling River discovery separately; the Agno ARB7 Paniqui station is not Camiling River evidence.
Keep Central Luzon and Luzon incomplete until all habitat lanes, evidence, rights and per-waterbody coverage gates are reconciled.

sources.supports: Conference date, abstract citation/authors, basin/locality wording and aggregate claims as printed.
Later article's author list, aggregate results, station list, sampling dates/methods and CC BY license.
Linked dataset identity, available station-level data description and CC BY 4.0 declaration.
